It has become a landmark for travellers, not just because of its strategic location, but also due to the experience it delivers.

The first thing you notice as you arrive at HFM is the spacious, well-organized parking area, which makes it very convenient for cars, buses, and even larger vehicles. The ambiance of the mall is modern yet welcoming, making it a pleasant break point for families, friends, and solo travellers alike.

One of the biggest highlights of HFM is the sheer variety of food options available. Inside the mall, you will find popular franchises like Hocco, Dayro, Starbucks, Subway, Bole to Mumbai, The Shake Maker, Dominos, Panch Ratna’s, and So South. Whether you’re craving authentic South Indian dishes, cheesy pizzas, refreshing shakes, or premium coffee, there’s something for every taste and mood. The washrooms are well-maintained, hygienic, and regularly cleaned, which makes a huge difference during long journeys. Handwashing and sanitization facilities are conveniently available, reflecting the mall’s attention to detail and customer comfort.

HFM is not just about food – it’s about an experience. Whether you are stopping for a quick coffee, enjoying a hearty meal, or simply stretching your legs, the atmosphere here feels lively yet relaxing. The décor is modern, lighting is warm, and the entire space feels safe and family-friendly.

Another plus point is that HFM caters to all budgets. From affordable snacks to premium dining, travellers can choose according to their preference without compromising on quality.

Overall, Highway Food Mall at Limbdi is a must-visit stop for anyone travelling through this route. Its combination of variety, hygiene, convenience, and friendly service ensures that every visit leaves you refreshed and satisfied. Once you experience HFM, it’s hard to imagine a highway journey without making a stop here.

Chotila Chamunda Mata Temple is not just a journey, but a deeply spiritual experience. Situated atop the hill, the temple dedicated to Maa Chamunda radiates immense positivity and devotion.
Reaching the temple requires climbing around 650–700 steps, but the spiritual energy and devotion around make the journey feel meaningful. Throughout the climb, devotees chanting “Jai Mata Di” create a divine atmosphere that keeps you motivated.
We visited in December, so thankfully the weather was pleasant and we did not feel much heat during the climb, which made the experience even more comfortable.
Once you reach the top, the feeling is truly peaceful and blessed. The view from the temple is mesmerizing, offering a beautiful panoramic sight that makes the entire climb worth it.
Another beautiful part of the experience is the free Mahaprasad served at the ground floor temple premises. Do check the timings if you plan to have it.
The temple premises are well managed considering the large number of devotees visiting daily. Early morning or evening visits feel especially calm and spiritual.
Whether you visit for devotion, peace of mind, or spiritual connection, Chotila Temple leaves you with positivity, gratitude, and inner strength.
A truly divine and memorable experience. 🙏
